radiusSource: Radius 1.26 +/- 0.03 Jupiter radii, the estimate Sutlieff et al. GM from their model mass 2.4 +/- 0.6 Jupiter masses times Jupiter's GM 126686531.9 km^3/s^2; no dynamical mass is measured. A sphere.
orbitalPeriodSource: Derived: Kepler's third law with the published semi-major axis 26.0 +2.2/-6.1 au (Sutlieff et al. 2026, Table 2, non-orbit-crossing posteriors) and the system mass 1.75 solar masses (Lacour et al. 2021) plus the three planets' 11.90, 8.89 and 2.4 Jupiter masses: 99.59 yr = 36374.8 d. The paper's own period posterior is 91 +18/-27 yr; a free circular fit to its six epochs gives 94.5 yr.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the model radius in the shared neutral gray, self-luminous. No image, visible colour, map or oblateness of Beta Pictoris d is measured; its size comes from its luminosity and models, its mass and orbit from astrometry.

effectiveTemperatureSource: 600 +45/-60 K, Sutlieff et al. (2026, arXiv:2606.23801, Table 2), estimated from the photometry with evolutionary models.
semiMajorAxisSource: Sutlieff et al. (2026, Table 2): a 26.0 +2.2/-6.1 au at 19.63 pc (1324.2 mas), 3598.36 radii of the star's 1,080,920 km; inclination 89.0 +0.7/-0.6 degrees. Eccentricity is set to 0: the paper bounds it below 0.44 (2 sigma) without a median, so this record is a circular display approximation, not the paper's orbital solution.
